newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan approves oil-fuelled power generator.
newsitem.headline: Japan approves oil-fuelled power generator.

text.p: A Japanese government panel approved the construction an oil-fuelled thermal power generator for the first time in 13 years, an Economic Planning Agency official said on Thursday.
Chubu Electric Power's one million kilowatt (kw) fuel oil-fired generator will be built in central Japan's Aichi prefecture and will start commercial operation between 2001 to 2003.

The decision to build an oil-fuelled generator does not infringe a 1979 International Energy Agency (IEA) recommendation that stipulates that construction of oil-fuelled plants to cover base demand should be avoided with a few exceptions, the official said.
Chubu's new unit will be used only when power demand peaks, he said.
When the new generator comes on line, Chubu said it will scrap some of its aging oil-burning power generators.
The government panel also approved Chubu's plans to build two coal-fired reactors with a combined capacity of two million kw.
Other than Chubu's three generators, the government panel approved the construction of a six power plants with total capacity of 11.12 million kw, the official said.
The panel also approved Kansai Electric Power Co Inc's plans to build two plants -- a 4.4 million-kw power plant that runs on orimulsion and a 3.7 million-kw, natural gas-powered power station.
Orimulsion is a tar-like fuel made up of water and bitumen.
The two plants, to be located in western Japan's Wakayama prefecture, are due to start commercial operation by 2007.

Electric Power Development Co Ltd's plans for a 20,000-kw geothermal power plant and two hydroelectric plants with a total capacity of 1.8 million kw, and Kyushu Electric Power Co Inc's 1.2 million kw hydroelectric power plant, were also given approval.
